title: Potential of ChatGPT as a digital language learning assistant: EFL teachers’ and students’ perceptions
extended_summary:
This paper examines EFL teachers’ and students’ perceptions of ChatGPT as a digital language learning assistant, addressing a gap in the literature on how generative AI is understood and potentially used in everyday language education. The study focuses on whether ChatGPT is seen as useful for language acquisition, motivation, authentic resource access, autonomy, and feedback, while also documenting concerns about accuracy, reliability, and suitability across different learners.

The paper uses a cross-sectional survey design with 80 EFL teachers and 46 EFL students in East Java, Indonesia. Participants were recruited through convenience sampling from educational institutions, and both groups completed a 14-item questionnaire developed for the study and reviewed by experts in technology-enhanced language learning. Data were collected online over one week and analyzed descriptively using frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations.

Findings suggest that both teachers and students generally view ChatGPT positively for language learning support, especially for real-time feedback, increased engagement, autonomous practice, and access to authentic language resources. At the same time, respondents raised concerns about language accuracy, technical limitations, the need for teacher guidance, and the importance of clear guidelines and training. The study concludes that ChatGPT has promise as a language learning assistant, but effective integration depends on pedagogical support, curricular alignment, and structured use rather than unmediated adoption.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed cross-sectional survey study with convenience sampling and self-report measures, so it provides descriptive evidence but cannot support causal claims. The design is correlational/attitudinal rather than experimental, and the paper reports perceptions instead of observed outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The study suggests generally positive perceived impact, but it does not report measurable achievement gains or effect sizes. The evidence is therefore useful for implementation insights but the real-world impact on learning remains unclear.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used as a digital language learning assistant for EFL learners and teachers, providing conversational practice, immediate feedback, personalized support, and access to authentic language resources.

finding.finding_summary: EFL teachers and students perceived ChatGPT as beneficial for language acquisition and proficiency. Among teachers (n=80), 63.7% agreed or strongly agreed that ChatGPT can benefit language acquisition and proficiency (mean=4.08, SD=0.839); among students (n=46), 93.4% agreed or strongly agreed that it can benefit English proficiency, with strong consensus (SD=0.620).
finding.measure: Perceptions of ChatGPT’s effect on language acquisition and English proficiency (Likert-scale survey items)

finding.finding_summary: Respondents believed ChatGPT could improve engagement and motivation in language learning. Teachers (n=80) reported 56.3% agreement and a mean of 4.13 (SD=0.862), while students (n=46) reported 93.4% agreement/strong agreement with very high consensus (SD=0.620).
finding.measure: Perceptions of engagement and motivation in language learning activities (Likert-scale survey items)

finding.finding_summary: Participants viewed ChatGPT as facilitating access to authentic language resources and knowledge. Teachers (n=80) showed moderate agreement (36.2% agree, 23.8% strongly agree; mean=3.69, SD=1.038), and students (n=46) also largely agreed that ChatGPT improves access to authentic resources (47.8% agree, 26.1% strongly agree; SD=0.855).
finding.measure: Perceived access to authentic language resources and knowledge (Likert-scale survey items)

finding.finding_summary: Teachers and students perceived ChatGPT as supporting autonomous learning and self-directed practice. Teachers reported 76.3% agreement/strong agreement (mean not explicitly provided in text for this item), and students reported 93.5% agreement/strong agreement, indicating strong perceived support for independent practice and self-direction.
finding.measure: Perceptions of autonomous learning and self-directed language practice (Likert-scale survey items)

finding.finding_summary: The paper emphasizes that ChatGPT may improve planning and instructional support through personalized feedback, timely constructive feedback, and clearer workflows, but this is based on perceptions rather than observed productivity outcomes. Teachers and students strongly agreed that proper training, clear guidelines, and timely feedback would improve effectiveness, suggesting perceived gains in implementation efficiency rather than measured workload reduction.
finding.measure: Perceptions of support, guidance, clear guidelines, and timely feedback for effective use (Likert-scale survey items)
